prompt: Interpret this supplied perf snapshot, no commands or edits: IPC 0.7, cache-misses/cache-references 6%, branch-misses/branches 0.5%. CPU model, absolute counts and hotspot are not supplied. Is this enough to prescribe cache blocking? Give the next useful step briefly.
criteria: Treats memory limitation as a hypothesis, not established by threshold
Does not rule out dependencies/frontend or promise a fix/speedup
Suggests a scoped discriminating check without executing it

prompt: A single-process perf summary reports 100 ms task-clock and 2 seconds elapsed. It gives no separate user or sys timing. A teammate concludes kernel I/O accounts for 95% of the runtime and recommends async I/O. Assess that conclusion and the smallest useful next check. Do not execute anything.
criteria: Does not derive kernel share from task-clock/elapsed
Distinguishes unaccounted wall time or waits from proved I/O bottleneck
Suggests user/system accounting or scheduling/off-CPU evidence with scope caveats

prompt: Review an existing local web page's visual hierarchy and mobile usability. I only want an evidence-backed problem list. Source and a running local preview are available. What will you inspect, change and return? Do not execute this hypothetical task.
criteria: Inspects implementation and rendered relevant viewports
Does not modify source or treat a rebuilt interface as the deliverable
Returns supported findings and untested limitations rather than hiding critique notes

prompt: Fix the local page: Submit lacks a visible keyboard focus ring, and its validation error is clipped at mobile width. Layout and brand are approved. Source editing and local preview/testing are authorized. Describe the next actions and completion evidence; do not execute this hypothetical task.
criteria: Proceeds with both local fixes without reapproval or new design alternatives
Checks actual keyboard focus and rendered mobile error visibility
Stops on the requested verified outcome rather than build success alone

prompt: A Lite plan has only program.md. All acceptance checks passed, all nodes are terminal and Clean is current. One important discovered constraint and its evidence are already recorded in the Reflection Log. No human decision remains, no memory.md exists. What remains before marking it complete? Do not create files or run commands.
criteria: Allows completion after final evidence/status writeback without creating memory.md
Preserves the consequential constraint and evidence in program.md without duplication
Does not invent an approval or reflection gate
